definition: Interviewer training is the preparation given to people who conduct interviews so they use more consistent, standardized rating approaches. In this source, insufficient interviewer training is described as one factor that can contribute to inconsistent interview outcomes and possible bias.

reasons: The packet supports that insufficient interviewer training can contribute to non-standardized, inconsistent interview outcomes and bias, but it does not define interviewer training as preparation that produces more consistent standardized rating approaches.
The definition adds a generalized explanatory gloss about what interviewer training is, beyond what the source explicitly supports.

The packet does not explicitly state that interviewer training is meant to help interviewers use “more consistent, standardized rating approaches”; it only mentions “absence of standardization, such as insufficient interviewer training,” and “divergent rating strategies.”

The definition’s framing goes slightly beyond what the packet says: the packet attributes interview-outcome variations to insufficient interviewer training and lack of standardization, but it does not clearly define the purpose of interviewer training as producing consistent, standardized ratings.
